user_scenario:
You are Wendell Pokorny, sixty-seven, who has raised corn and fed cattle near St. Paul, Nebraska since the early eighties. You are calling Cottonwood Plains Farm Credit on Wednesday morning, July 22, 2026, from the pickup, in no particular hurry and in plain words. A neighbor has offered you his quarter section and you want to free up cash toward the down payment. What you want today is to put in a request to redeem as much of your Class H preferred stock as the association's rules allow while keeping the preferred account open; you do not want it closed, and you have no idea what that figure comes to, so you ask the agent to work it out from your records. You are fine with the agent taking care of whatever the association handles on its side, but the redemption request itself is yours to sign, so when the agent hands it to you, you submit it yourself for exactly the amount the agent tells you.

When asked who you are, you give your phone number, 7854651873. When the agent wants to verify you, you read off your member number, CPF-5274409, from the patronage notice on the dash; if one more detail is needed, the last four of your Social Security number are 8461. Only if asked for an email is it wendell.pokorny@gmail.com, and only if asked when you joined, it was February 17, 2009, so 2009-02-17. Any money the association pays you on the preferred stock goes to your checking account ending 5306; you confirm that if the agent asks where it should go.

You do not volunteer anything else about your preferred stock. Only if the agent asks whether you sent anything in earlier about it do you say yes, you mailed a signed letter in early June asking to redeem six hundred thousand dollars and figured it was being taken care of. If the agent explains that something on your preferred stock has to be booked or paid first, you say that is fine, go ahead, and you wait while it is done; if the agent tells you an amount that was paid or booked, you just say all right, you trust the record. If the agent quotes the amount you can ask to redeem, you do not argue it or offer a different number, and when the agent hands you the redemption request, you submit it for that amount and read back the request reference you are given if asked. Once the agent tells you the request is in, you thank them and hang up.
